What We Do

Full-Service EMS & Ambulance Revenue Cycle Management

Ambulance billing is one of the most regulated specialties in U.S. healthcare, ALS vs. BLS level determination, loaded mile billing, non-emergency transport medical necessity, and Medicare ambulance fee schedule rules all running simultaneously. PMEX manages every element from PCR to payment.

ALS/BLS Level Coding

ALS1, ALS2, BLS emergency and non-emergency levels coded from the PCR.

Mileage Billing

Loaded miles (A0425) billed per the trip sheet, unloaded miles excluded.

Non-Emergency Transport

Medical necessity documentation compiled for non-emergency trips.

Medicare Ambulance Rules

Closest appropriate facility and origin/destination modifier compliance.

Intercept Billing

ALS intercept (A0426) coded when BLS unit meets ALS unit en route.

Patient Balance Collection

Patient statements and self-pay follow-up managed within PMEX.

Sound Familiar?

Common Ambulance (EMS) Billing Problems, and How PMEX Fixes Them

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

ALS1 vs. BLS determination wrong, higher level not billed from PCR documentation.

PMEX codes ALS or BLS from the documented interventions in the PCR, not crew designation alone.

Mileage billed as round-trip miles instead of loaded miles only.

PMEX bills loaded miles only from point of patient contact to destination per the trip odometer.

Non-emergency transport denied, physician certification statement not on file.

PMEX collects the PCS before billing every non-emergency transport as a pre-billing requirement.

Medicare closest-facility rule not applied, farther transport not documented.

PMEX confirms and documents the closest-appropriate-facility rationale before submission.

ALS intercept not billed when BLS unit initiated and ALS met en route.

PMEX identifies every intercept from the PCR and bills A0426 alongside the BLS transport claim.

Patient self-pay balances written off without collection follow-up.

PMEX manages patient statements and self-pay follow-up within standard collection workflows.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Ambulance Billing, and How PMEX Fixes Them

EMS agencies lose 18–30% of collectible revenue to preventable billing errors. These three patterns generate the majority of ambulance claim denials.

PATTERN 01

ALS Level Undercoded, BLS Billed When ALS Services Were Provided

Paramedic administered IV medication and performed cardiac monitoring. Billed as BLS emergency (A0429, $320). Correct: ALS1 emergency (A0427, $480). $160 per transport lost when ALS services are documented but not coded.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX reviews every PCR for ALS-qualifying interventions, IV access, advanced airway, cardiac monitoring, medication administration, and codes the correct level from documented interventions.

PATTERN 02

Non-Emergency Transport Denied, PCS Not Obtained

Dialysis transport claim submitted. Medicare denies, no Physician Certification Statement on file attesting bed-confinement. $280 per trip permanently lost without the PCS.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX manages PCS collection as a pre-transport workflow, confirming the signed statement is on file before billing the non-emergency trip.

PATTERN 03

Mileage Overbilled, Round-Trip Miles Submitted

Transport from scene to hospital: 12 loaded miles. Billing team submits 24 miles (round trip). Medicare allows loaded miles only. Overpayment creates recoupment exposure on audit.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX bills loaded miles only, from point of patient contact to destination, per the trip odometer readings in the PCR.

Ambulance Billing Questions Answered

ALS1 requires an ALS assessment or one ALS intervention. ALS2 requires three or more ALS interventions or drug administration from the paramedic-level formulary. We code from PCR interventions documented.

Yes, if the patient is bed-confined and no other transportation method is medically appropriate. A Physician Certification Statement must be on file before billing.

We apply the correct HCPCS modifier pair from the transport record, SH (scene to hospital), HH (hospital to hospital), etc., per CMS ambulance fee schedule rules.

Yes. A0426 (ALS intercept) is separately billable when a BLS unit initiates transport and an ALS unit meets the patient en route to provide ALS care.

We work with ESO, ImageTrend, Rescue 1, EPCR platforms, and paper PCR systems.
